summary: Build a standalone warehouse admin UI — a new React + Vite SPA in the same tech stack as the existing Bob pipeline web app — that provides CRUD screens for the domain-model classes in the Java source tree, starting with Vehicle.
approach: Create two sibling npm workspace packages under tools/: a Fastify REST server (tools/warehouse-server) persisting warehouse entities in a local SQLite database via node:sqlite, and a React 18 + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4 + React Router v6 + React Query v5 SPA (tools/warehouse-ui) with list, create, edit and delete screens for Vehicle. The packages follow the same conventions as the existing tools/bob-pipeline apps. No existing file is changed except the workspace config to register the two new packages.

alternatives_considered.option: Extend the existing pipeline web app with warehouse pages
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The pipeline UI is tightly coupled to the Bob pipeline domain; mixing warehouse admin into it conflates unrelated concerns and makes both harder to navigate.

alternatives_considered.option: Use a full Spring Boot or Quarkus backend
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Adds a build system and runtime dependency not present in the repo; the pipeline server already proves Node + Fastify + SQLite is sufficient for a local admin tool.

alternatives_considered.option: Generate a UI from the Java classes via reflection
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: No build system exists and there is no JVM process running to reflect against; the Java classes are compiled independently.

components: tools/warehouse-server — new Fastify REST API: CRUD endpoints per entity, SQLite persistence, serves built SPA as static files
tools/warehouse-ui — new React SPA: list, create, edit, delete screens for Vehicle; shared UI primitives matching the pipeline web app
src/main/java/com/neversoft/vehicle/Vehicle.java — not modified; defines the canonical domain shape the warehouse server mirrors in TypeScript types
assumptions: The phrase 'same tech stack as the sales orders' refers to the Bob pipeline web app (tools/bob-pipeline/apps/web), the only existing UI in the repository.
Other warehouse classes are the Java domain POJOs in src/main/java/; Vehicle (issue #1) is the only class currently present, so it is the first entity type the admin UI covers.
Additional entity types added by future issues will be handled in follow-up issues; this issue covers Vehicle only.
The warehouse admin UI is a local developer tool requiring no authentication beyond the developer's workstation.
Node 22.13+ is available (required for node:sqlite, consistent with the pipeline server requirement).

risks.risk: 'Warehouse classes' turns out to mean something other than the Java POJOs in src/
risks.mitigation: Confirm with the issue author; the plan is easy to pivot if the target entities differ.

risks.risk: Node 22.13+ node:sqlite not available on the developer's machine
risks.mitigation: Mirror the pipeline server's existing approach: check at startup and emit a clear error message.

risks.risk: Duplicated UI primitives drift from the pipeline web app over time
risks.mitigation: Extract shared components to a new tools/bob-pipeline/packages/ui package in a future cleanup; out of scope here.

risks.risk: Vite port conflict between warehouse-ui dev server and pipeline web app dev server
risks.mitigation: Use a distinct default port (e.g. 4322) in vite.config.ts.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A new npm workspace package tools/warehouse-ui exists, built with Vite + React 18 + Tailwind CSS v4 + React Router v6 + React Query v5, matching the dependency versions in tools/bob-pipeline/apps/web/package.json.

A new npm workspace package tools/warehouse-server exists with a Fastify server that listens on 127.0.0.1 and serves CRUD REST endpoints: GET /api/vehicles, GET /api/vehicles/:id, POST /api/vehicles, PUT /api/vehicles/:id, DELETE /api/vehicles/:id.
The warehouse server persists Vehicle records to a local SQLite database using node:sqlite (Node 22.13+), with columns matching Vehicle.java fields: id, make, model, year, vin, color, mileage.

The warehouse UI displays a paginated/filterable list of vehicles, a create form, an edit form, and a delete confirmation, using the same visual primitives (Card, Button, Tailwind classes) as the pipeline web app.
The warehouse UI's Vite dev server proxies /api requests to the warehouse server, not the pipeline server.
npm run typecheck passes with zero errors in both new packages.
No existing file in the repository is modified except the root package.json (or monorepo workspace config) to register the two new packages.

open_questions: Should the warehouse server share the same SQLite database file as the pipeline server, or use its own? (Recommendation: its own, to keep concerns separated.)
Are there other domain entity types beyond Vehicle that should be scaffolded in this issue, or should only Vehicle be covered now?
